gaps.note: Eleven networks had no network unit in cycle 12. On them the only new evidence is pmdiff6 (theme-bytecode-coverage) and, for 4663, 99901, 143, 4326, 5042 and 43114, mined removals (theme-mined-liquidity-2). The battery, targeted set and MULMOD sequence vectors of established-l1 were not rerun there, and no release note or fix commit since the versions OPCODES.md records was read for reth v2.11.0, celo reth, xlayer-reth, Nitro, Monad, mega-reth, Tempo, Arc or HyperEVM. Critic query of web3_clientVersion on 2026-11-24 against the endpoints in state/networks.json: reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc (1), reth/v2.2.0-74cc8bb (42220), reth/v2.3.0-f60420a/xlayer/v0.0.7 (196), nitro/v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f-20261116T155937Z/linux-arm64/go1.27.3 (42161 and 4663), nitro/vlocal+unknown-unknown/go1.25.12 (99901), Monad/0.16.7 (143), mega-reth/v2.2.3-72527bc (4326), tempo/v1.19.0-697ea97 (4217), arc/v1 (5042), hyperliquid evm Mainnet (999). The versions match what earlier cycles recorded, so the gap is reading, not version drift.

theme-code-cache-consistency read the Nitro jump destination cache at v3.12.4 (go-ethereum fork 0e44603): a BlockChain-owned LRU of eight shards keyed by code hash, shared across blocks and the parallel prefetcher. Both endpoints report v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f, a tag that is not public (cycle 11 arbitrum-family got 404 for go.mod at v3.13.0 and v3.13.0-rc.9). The clearance therefore describes a release that the answering nodes do not run, and nobody read whether the fork's master branch changed core/jumpdest.go, the prefetcher, or the cache's lifetime across reorgs since 0e44603.

Monad. L-648 stays inconclusive: whether the 24,009 byte runtime is ever compiled depends on asmjit text size, which nobody computed. The 83 branches that pmdiff6 newly covers (clear, allowance, hook return-delta flags, SqrtPriceMath fallback, the 2^128 fee branch) ran only in the interpreter on Monad, because eth_call there never runs native code. theme-proof-builds reports the release page lists v0.16.5 for mainnet and v0.16.7 for testnet only, while rpc.monad.xyz answers Monad/0.16.7 (critic query above), so which release produces blocks is still not established.

Proof builds. theme-proof-builds settled OP Mainnet, Unichain, Ink, World Chain, Zora and Soneium. Base respects game type 621 (AggregateVerifier with a Nitro TEE image and an SP1 range program), whose embedded EVM and integer library versions are unread, and the game types of Celo and X Layer were not read at all.

BNB Smart Chain. Every source reading of cycles 8 to 12 (interpreter, process-wide jump destination LRU, keccak, prefetcher) is of the public v1.8.2 tag 54afaff, while bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org runs commit 4e1c8247, which is not in the public repository (established-l1 finding 0). The clearance of L-646 for BSC rests on the tag.

Arc answers arc/v1 with no commit, and the F-032 verifier recorded that Arc keeps a custom SELFDESTRUCT in crates/evm/src/opcode.rs. No unit has read Arc's instruction table override as a whole, at any version, to list which opcodes Arc replaces and whether any replacement touches CALL with value, BALANCE, SELFBALANCE or the copy and storage opcodes the PoolManager uses.

The MegaETH sequencer executor and the HyperEVM validator are closed. Neither the analysis or compiled code cache question of L-645/L-646 nor the opcode battery can reach them; only mined results do, and those cover common values.

leads.question: Monad v0.16.7 removed the YP K.1 ripemd touch from execute_message.cpp with the comment that reverted state depends on whether the bytecode was executed as compiled native code or interpreted (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/execution/ethereum/execute_message.cpp lines 150-160, fetched by the critic; v0.16.5 lines 150-155 still touch). In v0.16.5 and v0.16.7, which state can differ between the two paths after a frame reverts or runs out of gas: transient storage writes, storage writes, touched and warm sets, logs, refund counter, created accounts, balances? Read the compiled runtime's out-of-gas and revert exits (block-level gas checks before a basic block runs, the TSTORE and SSTORE runtime calls and their journal entries) and the interpreter's. Then say whether a reverted inner frame of an unlockCallback that runs sync, a token transfer to the PoolManager and settle can leave a CurrencyDelta credit (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/PoolManager.sol:349-364) or a synced currency (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32) on one path after the transfer itself was rolled back.
leads.why: A credit that survives a revert while the payment does not would let any account take pooled tokens it never paid, on pools with no attacker hook or token. Monad's developers state that reverted state is path dependent, and cycle 11 checked only that TSTORE uses the same journal, not every exit of compiled code.

leads.question: Which Monad release do mainnet block producers run on 2026-11-24 (validator docs, the release page, monad-bft or validator announcements), and on that release is the PoolManager runtime compiled at all? If a build of the emitter is not possible, can mined data answer it: does gas used by identical PoolManager calls in mined receipts differ before and after the code hash has consumed max_code_size(10,240 + 32 x 24,009) gas of interpretation on a node?
leads.why: Every Monad opcode result for the compiled path rests on transcription. If producers compile the PoolManager, the 83 newly covered branches and every settlement branch have no network evidence on the code blocks run.

leads.question: For nitro v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f, which go-ethereum fork commit does the nitro master branch pin today (raw go-ethereum submodule reference or go.mod replace in OffchainLabs/nitro master), and do core/jumpdest.go, core/vm/contract.go and the prefetcher in that commit differ from 0e44603 in how the cache key is derived, whether the prefetcher writes the cache from a speculative StateDB, and whether entries survive a reorg or an EIP-7702 redelegation of the same address?
leads.why: The Nitro cache is shared across blocks and the prefetcher. A key not derived from the analysed bytes would let one bytecode's bitmap judge the PoolManager's jumps on the sequencer, which freezes or misroutes every PoolManager call.

leads.question: From mined blocks, list the PoolManager branches that pmdiff6 newly covered (clear of an exact delta, finite and infinite allowance in transferFrom and burn, hook return-delta flags, hook self-calls, the SqrtPriceMath overflow fallback and the 2^128 fee branch) that appear in at least one mined transaction on Monad, MegaETH and HyperEVM, using debug_traceTransaction call frames where served. For each branch with a mined instance, does the receipt and storage equal a rerun in pyevm.py from the parent state?
leads.why: On these three networks the code that produces blocks is not the code that answers eth_call, so pmdiff6 says nothing about the producer for these credit-deciding branches.

leads.question: OPCODES.md records 85,278 of 88,576 mined swap pairs matching single-step formulas and the rest attributed to multi-step swaps. op-stack-eth found that 4 Ink swaps reported as not reproduced were a missing tick spacing (90) in replay.py SPACINGS. After reading the spacing from the Initialize event or the swap calldata, does every unmatched pair on every network replay to the unit, and which ones still do not?
leads.why: The Ink case shows that some non-matches were never explained, only attributed. A residual unmatched swap on one network is the most direct trace a planted arithmetic difference would leave.

leads.question: Base respects game type 621, an AggregateVerifier with a Nitro TEE image hash 0x73181275... and an SP1 range program hash 0x3d3713d3... (theme-proof-builds lead). Which published release produces those hashes, which revm, ruint and alloy-primitives versions does the range program embed, and can any account call challenge() with a ZK proof?
leads.why: If the proof program computes an opcode differently and anyone can challenge, an ordinary transaction could make honest output roots disputable and stall withdrawals of bridged pool funds.

leads.question: In the Arc node source (circlefin arc-node, crates/evm/src/opcode.rs and the instruction table builder), list every opcode Arc replaces or wraps relative to revm, and for each one say whether the PoolManager runtime executes it (CALL with value at src/types/Currency.sol:48, BALANCE or SELFBALANCE at src/types/Currency.sol:92, TSTORE, MCOPY, RETURNDATACOPY) and whether the replacement can return another result or another success flag.
leads.why: Arc is the one network known to override an opcode handler. Arc's endpoint reports no commit, and no unit has read the override set as a whole.

leads.question: On mips64 without native 128 bit multiply and divide, which routines does ruint 1.20.0 (as pinned by kona-client 1.9.0) use for the 64x64 to 128 products and 128 by 64 divisions behind MULMOD, MUL and DIV (compiler-builtins __multi3 and __udivti3, or ruint's own algorithms), and do the targeted and battery vectors pass through a Python transcription of those routines?
leads.why: theme-proof-builds transcribed op-program on MIPS64 for World Chain but not the Rust path that OP Mainnet, Unichain and Ink now settle on. A mismatch would make an honest output root disputable.

leads.question: Which game type do the DisputeGameFactory contracts of Celo and X Layer respect today (respectedGameType on the OptimismPortal, gameImpls on the factory, read by eth_call on Ethereum), and which program and integer library does it embed?
leads.why: Closes the last two OP Stack style networks whose settled state no unit has tied to a build.

leads.question: Monad's staking precompile at 0x1000 consumes all gas on a failing call. Which precompiles or system contracts on HyperEVM, Tempo and Celo also consume all forwarded gas on a failed call, and can any of them be reached by the PoolManager inside a transaction that a victim sends (a victim router, not an attacker pool)?
leads.why: Hook and transfer calls forward all gas (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, src/types/Currency.sol:48 and 73). Reaching one from a victim's own transaction would let an attacker make that transaction fail; reaching it only from the attacker's own transaction is harmless.
